# docs/memory/data/

<!-- Generated by php tools/memory_index.php from the frontmatter of each file, except the key rules between the two marker lines, which are written by hand. -->

Table structures and SQL pitfalls.

## Key rules

<!-- key-rules:start -->
- New code runs a query with values through `db_q($sql, array($v, …))` (`?` placeholders), not `mysqli_query()`; it returns `false` on failure like `mysqli_query()`, so keep the caller's check (`db-q-placeholder-helper.md`).
- Escape every value with `e()`; in LIKE write `e(escape_like($v))`: `escape_like()` alone escapes no quote and is an SQL injection (`db-helpers-and-error-contract.md`).
- Never compare an INT column with `''` (every row that belongs to nothing matches) or a DATE column with `''` (use `'0000-00-00'`); check a LEFT JOIN id first (`sql-silent-wrong-results.md`).
- Read with a one-shape helper (`db_value`, `db_values`, `db_item`, `db_items`): `db()`'s answer changes with the row count, so a loop over it breaks on one row (`db-helpers-and-error-contract.md`).
- Probe a table or column a migration adds with `pg_schema_has()` behind a readiness function before reading it (`sql-silent-wrong-results.md`).
- Write `orders` with `generate_order_reference_code()`, an ENUM-valid `payment_method` and an `order_date`; run nothing between the `next_order_number` lock and unlock (`orders-table-write-traps.md`).
- Validate first, write after, when a write spans tables: any table may still be MyISAM, which has no transactions and survives a rollback (`table-engines-and-row-size.md`).
- Add no VARCHAR to `config` (TEXT only); on a wide InnoDB table prefer TEXT or VARCHAR(64)+ to short VARCHARs (`config-table-no-varchar.md`).
- Bring a URL name to ASCII (`prepare_file_name()`, `pg_transliterate_to_ascii()`), transliterating before `mb_strtolower()`; rename the file on disk before `files.name` (`slug-generation.md`).
<!-- key-rules:end -->
